top.title: Chiefs Veteran LB Discusses Contract Restructuring
top.description: Nick Bolton is one of the Kansas City Chiefs’ captains for a reason. He has showcased his leadership and selflessness throughout the years, always thinking of what’s best for the team. The veteran linebacker addressed the franchise’s trade deadline decision on Thursday, He entered the NFL as Kansas City’s No. 58 overall pick in the second round in 2021. Bolton starred for the Missouri Tigers in college from 2018-2020, earning second-team All-American in his final year and was a two time first-team All-SEC selection. The 26-year-old has spent his entire professional career with the Chiefs. He has 692 combined tackles consisting of 291 assisted and 401 solo efforts, along with 6.0 sacks. Bolton also has five interceptions, 23 pass deflections, 25 QB hits and 46 tackles for loss under his name. Kansas City Chiefs linebackers Nick Bolton, Drue Tranquill and Jaylen Watsoncelebrate after a turnover on downs against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs Veteran LB Discusses Contract Restructuring Nick Bolton addressed the media on Thursday. He talked about his contract getting restructured to create cap space for Josh Downs, who the team traded for ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. The two-time Super Bowl champion made it clear that he didn’t mind it at all as long as it helps the franchise. “My agent called me a couple days prior,” Bolton said. “Obviously, we’re trying to make a move and they just need a little bit more space. So like I said, we can bring in good players and hope our team win football games. I’m all for it. But that’s pretty much all it was. A couple days of communication just giving me a heads up that this might happen or it’s an opportunity could happen. And obviously, we could bring good guys in the building. I’m all for it.” Nick Bolton on restructuring to clear space for Josh Downs: “My agent called me a couple days prior… They just need a little bit more space so we can bring in good players… I’m all for it.” Captain move. | Chiefs on YouTube https://t.co/6EMJ4aiggY — Daily Chiefs (@Daily_Chiefs_) November 12, 2026 Downs addresses the Chiefs’ need for another wide receiver. top.title: Ma'asi-White marks landmark with try in Sale win
top.description: Rekeiti Ma'asi-White made his England A debut against New Zealand A last season [Getty Images] Prem Rugby Cup Sale (14) 38 Tries: Wills, Ma'asi-White, Longstaff, Jibulu 2, penalty try Cons: Davies 3 Exeter (12) 24 Tries: Poynton, Coen, McArthur, Wolstenholme Cons: Coen 2 Centre Rekeiti Ma'asi-White scored a try on his 50th appearance for Sale as the Sharks turned up the power to beat Exeter Chiefs and continue their impressive form in the Prem Rugby Cup. While the league campaign has been a struggle, Alex Sanderson's team have shown up well in Pool A and a bonus-point win at Corpacq Stadium stretched their lead at the top. Exeter struck first in the 11th minute with a try by left-wing Charlie Poynton, but Sale's response was instant as wing Alex Wills outjumped the Chiefs defence to grab a cross-kick and touch down. The sin-binning of Paul Brown-Bampoe for taking Wills out in the air gave the home side a man advantage for 10 minutes and they exploited it with a try by Ma'asi-White. Ben Coen had an opportunity to cut the deficit with a penalty, only to strike the post from 40 metres out, but the Exeter stand-off made amends with the last play of the half, stepping over from Zack Wimbush's pass to score the Chiefs' second try. Exeter, with 145kg prop Ehren Painter back and making his presence felt after almost two years out with a knee injury, were dominating the scrum but it was the Sharks' driving maul which came to the fore after the break to pull them clear. Three maul tries, one from hooker Alfie Longstaff and two for his replacement Nathan Jibulu did the damage with Sale adding a penalty try as Exeter illegally disrupted another drive close to their line. Hooker Max Norey was yellow-carded. Exeter did though manage a try-scoring bonus point with prop Archie McArthur and captain Sam Wolstenholme crossing in the second half to nudge them off the bottom of Pool A. top.title: Is Luke Fahey giving Ohio State its best chance to win?
top.description: The Ohio State Buckeyes are 6-3, No. 21 in the AP poll and coming off back-to-back losses to the USC Trojans and Oregon Ducks, the two games true freshman Luke Fahey has started since Julian Sayin hurt his arm against the Indiana Hoosiers on Oct. 17. Sayin is out for the rest of the regular season, and every week since, the quarterback conversation around the program has circled back to the five-star sitting behind Fahey on the depth chart. Ryan Day took that question at his weekly press conference Tuesday, ahead of Saturday’s noon ET game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium, and walked through how he got to his answer before giving it. Ryan Day’s Bold Claim of First and Second Rounders Reflects How Ohio State Gets Down, Says National Analyst (Imagn Images) “The first thing to know is we’re just gonna do whatever we can to win the game. What gives us the best chance to win the game? What gives the team the best chance to win it? And when we go through the process of making that decision, it ultimately is my decision, but I go through a lot of different channels to make sure that I’m getting really good feedback on what everybody else is seeing because it’s a big decision. So coaches, both sides of the ball, players, older guys, guys on offense, receivers, everybody, to find out what am I seeing here. Am I missing something? And so, Luke is gonna be our quarterback this week. Tavien’s one snap away. And that mentality has got to continue to be his mentality and continue to grow. And if we can continue to improve in practice and build enough trust within practice and if we feel like he gives us the best chance to win, we’ll make that move. We’re not at that point right now,” Day said . Is Luke Fahey giving Ohio State its best chance to win? Fahey went 21 of 38 for 260 yards and a touchdown in the 30-18 loss at USC on Oct. 31, then 36 of 50 for 360 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the 41-28 home loss to Oregon last Saturday. Ohio State averaged 438.5 yards across those two games and scored 46 points. Fans asking for St. Clair are working from those two Saturdays, and Day tied any change to what St. Clair shows on the practice field during the week. St. Clair, the five-star from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who signed in the 2025 class, has played 19 snaps in two games this season and is 5 of 7 for 52 yards with a touchdown and an interception. top.title: Unbeaten Utah’s Morgan Scalley addresses Kyle Whittingham’s struggles at Michigan in honest comments
top.description: Morgan Scalley’s first full season as head coach of the Utah Utes has them at 9-0, coming off a 28-20 win over the No. 9 BYU Cougars and holding the longest winning streak in FBS at 15 games. Two time zones east, the coach who handed him the program is having a far harder first season at a new job. Kyle Whittingham is 5-4 at the Michigan Wolverines and 2-4 in Big Ten play after a 15-6 home loss to the Michigan State Spartans on Nov. 7, against a team that came in at 2-5. Scalley was asked what Whittingham meant to him on The Triple Option podcast, in an interview released Thursday. Michigan football head coach Kyle Whittingham speaks as he is being introduced on the floor during the first half between Michigan and USC at Crisler Center in Ann Arbor on Friday, Jan. 2, 2026. “He gave me every opportunity I’ve had in coaching. He’s a guy that just believed in me. I loved him as a coach, as a person. He’s an amazing coach. I am feeling for what he’s going through. It’s unfortunate because obviously it’s a results-driven business, but people don’t really understand how great of a coach and person he is. Coaching, you go through good times, you go through bad times, and it’s not awesome, I’m sure, over there right now, and I feel for those coaches and their families, but I can’t say enough great things about Kyle Whittingham and what he’s done for me in my career. I would not be here in this seat if it wasn’t for Kyle Whittingham,” Scalley said. Morgan Scalley says he wouldn’t be where he is now without Kyle Whittingham https://t.co/uhPzUMN2Kw — The Triple Option (@3xOptionShow) November 12, 2026 How much of Utah’s unbeaten run traces back to Whittingham? Scalley spent 18 seasons on Whittingham’s staff, most of them as defensive coordinator, and Utah first named him coach-in-waiting in 2019 before formalizing it in July 2024. He took over a program coming off a 10-2 season, built over Whittingham’s 21 years and 177 wins in Salt Lake City. When Whittingham took the Michigan job on Dec. 26, most of his Utah assistants went with him. Only four stayed with Scalley: Colton Swan, who was promoted to defensive coordinator, running backs coach Mark Atuaia, defensive tackles coach Luther Elliss and cornerbacks coach Sharrieff Shah. Michigan’s year has had real wins, including one over then-No. 11 Oklahoma and another on the road at Penn State, along with losses to Iowa, Minnesota, Indiana and now Michigan State. Utah takes the nation’s longest winning streak into the final weeks of its Big 12 schedule, and Michigan has three regular-season games left in Whittingham’s first season, starting Saturday. top.title: NC State names ACC’s all-time passing leader Philip Rivers head coach on five-year deal
top.description: The NC State Wolfpack made Philip Rivers their head coach Friday after the university’s Board of Trustees approved a five-year contract in a morning meeting. The vote closed a search that had centered on the program’s most famous quarterback within days of Dave Doeren’s firing in October. Doeren, the program’s career wins leader with 98 victories, was let go midway through his 14th season. Rivers, 44, played 51 games for NC State from 2000 to 2003 and is still the ACC’s all-time leading passer. He has spent the last six seasons as head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, and he will be formally introduced Monday at a private event broadcast on ACC Network. Health insurance reset drives Philip Rivers comeback (Fox Sports) “I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University. In many ways, I feel like I’m coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. … I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. … There’s no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we’re not scared of hard,” Rivers said in a statement released by the school. Rivers is also the first football hire for Boo Corrigan as NC State’s athletic director. “Philip Rivers is one of one and the right person to lead NC State Football into its next era. His accomplishments as a player at the collegiate and professional levels speak for themselves. … Philip is a winner who embraces the high expectations we have for NC State Football,” Corrigan said . What Philip Rivers walks into at NC State The school did not release financial terms, but WRAL reported , citing a source, that Rivers will make $3.25 million a year. The team he takes over is 4-5 and coming off a 41-3 home loss to the Duke Blue Devils on Nov. 7. Interim coach Todd Goebbel will finish the season, starting with the Syracuse Orange in Raleigh on Saturday. His son, Gunner Rivers, a quarterback he has coached for three seasons at St. Michael, is already committed to NC State as the top recruit in its 2027 class. top.title: Everton In Brighton Race For 6ft 5in Defender: Can He Fix Moyes’ Back Line?
top.description: Everton In Brighton Race For 6ft 5in Defender: Can He Fix Moyes’ Back Line? Everton and Brighton are competing to sign Union Saint-Gilloise centre-back Massiré Sylla, according to Sport Witness , which cites Africa Foot. Both Premier League clubs have already made enquiries for the 21-year-old Senegalese, who also attracted earlier interest from AC Milan and recently signed a new contract at Union running until 2031. Sylla joined from Norwegian side Lyn in January and has since become a regular starter in Belgium. He has played 1,626 minutes across 18 appearances this season, and his market value has jumped to €5m, a little over £4m. At 6ft 5in and right-footed, Sylla wins headers, times his jumps well and threatens at set pieces. He steps out aggressively to win duels, reads danger well enough to intercept, and organises the players around him, with a passing range that includes long diagonals and the occasional line-breaking ball. The weaknesses are just as clear. His tackling can be mistimed, which lets quicker forwards slip past when he commits. He looks loose when a high ball arrives under pressure, and can lose his balance after contact. The Premier League will punish those habits far more often than Belgium does. That profile suits Everton ‘s situation. David Moyes has built a sixth-placed start of 16 points from 10 games on a defence that kept five clean sheets in its first seven league matches, yet James Tarkowski turns 34 next week, Michael Keane is 33, and Jarrad Branthwaite’s hamstring problems keep disrupting his availability. Both clubs are also chasing Atlético Mineiro’s Vitão, an 18-year-old Brazilian centre-back who stands 6ft 4in and won the 2025 CONMEBOL Under-17 Championship. He has only recently broken into Atlético’s senior side. Should Everton make Sylla their priority centre-back target? DUESSELDORF, GERMANY – OCTOBER 22: Massire Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between R. Union Saint-Gilloise and Hapoel Beer-Sheva FC at Merkur Spiel-Arena on October 22, 2026 in Duesseldorf, Germany. (Photo by Pau Barrena/Getty Images) Yes, and they should sign him as a first-team player, not a project. Tarkowski and Keane have both extended their contracts, but neither is getting quicker, and Branthwaite’s record makes him impossible to rely on. Sylla offers Moyes height at set pieces and a front-foot defender. His rash tackling would need coaching out of him, because Premier League wingers exploit a defender who lunges. Vitão is the less sensible chase. An 18-year-old with so little senior experience cannot cover for injuries this season, and Everton shouldn’t tie up a squad place on a player who needs two years. At a little over £4m, Sylla costs little enough that Everton can afford to be wrong, and that low risk should settle the argument.

top.description: UEFA Nations League: Dutch advance with big win before Olympiastadion test, Reis makes Slovakia debut The Netherlands are through to the last eight in the UEFA Nations League after their 7-0 victory over Greece in Amsterdam. The two teams started the day on equal points, but Xavi’s side produced a ruthless performance from start to finish. Borussia Dortmund's Joey Veerman provided the assist for the first of Tijani Reijnders’ three goals in the space of twenty first-half minutes. Fellow Saudi-based player Crysencio Summerville started the rout in the sixth minute, while ex-Borussia Dortmund attacker ended the scoring at the hour mark with the seventh goal of the night. On his return to the stadium of his former club, Arsenal’s Jurrien Timber also scored his first two goals for the Netherlands. Since the head-to-head record is the first tiebreaker, the hosts earned their spot in the knockout stage before their game against Germany at Olympiastadion on Monday night. Greece will simultaneously host Serbia in the other game from the group. If Germany and Greece win their respective games on the final matchday, all three teams will be tied on 11 points. If Germany manage to beat fierce rivals Dutch, they will advance to the knockout stage without having to wait for the other result. Serbia are yet to earn a point after their first five matches in League A of the competition. Meanwhile, Ludovit Reis, who played a total of 26 games for Netherlands youth national teams, made his Slovakia debut on Friday. The Werder Bremen midfielder played 85 minutes in the 2-2 draw with Faroe Islands for the League C3 leaders. Gregor Kobel (Dortmund), Fabian Rieder (Augsburg) and Michel Aebischer (Union Berlin) helped Switzerland to a goalless draw in Slovenia, which was enough to secure their promotion to League A with a game to spare.

top.title: Reijnders hat-trick fuels Dutch rout of Greece in Nations League
top.description: Tijjani Reijnders scored three times in the first half as the Dutch thumped Greece (Koen van Weel) Tijjani Reijnders scored a first-half hat-trick as the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 on Friday to move closer to securing a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Crysencio Summerville capitalised on a defensive lapse to give the Dutch an early lead in Amsterdam, before former Manchester City midfielder Reijnders doubled the advantage. Reijnders struck again from close range before completing his hat-trick in the 33rd minute when he squeezed home at the far post. Jurrien Timber turned in a Donyell Malen cross before half-time to make it 5-0, and the Arsenal defender added his second goal of the night on the hour mark. Malen completed the rout with a crisp first-time finish against a Greece side that bore little resemblance to the team that nearly beat the Netherlands last month. Greece had entered the match unbeaten in Group A2, having taken four points against Germany, and had held a two-goal lead against the Netherlands in October before Reijnders salvaged a 2-2 draw. Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side lead the way with 11 points, three clear of both Greece and Germany, going into the final round of group matches. Germany host the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday while Greece are at home to Serbia, who are without a point after five games. top.title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler is sending himself down to the G League for a game
top.description: Jimmy Butler III of the Golden State Warriors practices during half time of the Warriors game against the Memphis Grizzlies at Chase Center on Oct. 23, 2026, in San Francisco. (Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler says his first game back from his torn ACL will be in the G League. Butler tore his ACL on Jan. 19 and faced a year-long recovery process, but has been ramping up his activity in recent weeks. In an interview with the Athletic's Nick Friedell , Butler said he is planning on playing in a game with the Santa Cruz Warriors, Golden State's affiliate in the NBA minor league, as part of his rehabilitation process. "Well, y'all gonna get your opportunity come Santa Cruz," Butler told the Athletic. "Because I'm definitely coming down there to play. So good luck to everybody. Y'all ain't gonna get too many minutes out of me, but I'm definitely going down there. I want to hoop." Butler even acknowledged that there would be some who may not like the idea. Butler's agent Bernard Lee took to social media to voice his displeasure at Friedell for reporting the story. "Nick…you had to give this table legs huh?" Lee wrote on X . "I'm going to hit you with one of them when I see you." Within the organization, the main person who would be against the idea is Mike Dunleavy, the Warriors general manager and Butler's former teammate with the Bulls. When Friedell asked Butler if he had cleared the plan with Dunleavy, Friedell wrote Butler's smile only got bigger before responding. "I don't got to clear s-t with nobody," Butler said. "I'm going. Me and Mike will fistfight. He's gonna be like, ‘Jimmy, no.' I'm gonna be like, ‘Mike, yes. I'm going to G League, baby!' Y'all know where to find me. Santa Cruz, baby." One person who is clearly in favor of it, though, is Steve Kerr. In an interview with the Athletic in Houston on Wednesday, Kerr celebrated Butler's plans. "I think it makes such perfect sense," Kerr said. "But most guys in the league in Jimmy's position are, like, too vain to do it - and Jimmy's the opposite. I think he would love giving the fans down there a great surprise. That's amazing. I love that." Kerr related the move to how MLB players do rehab assignments in that sport's minor leagues. But while that is quite common in baseball, there has rarely been an NBA player who has done so. Warriors stars Steph Curry and Klay Thompson have both joined the "Sea Dubs" for practices during their recovery processes, but a star of Butler's stature has never played in a G League game. Kerr said if the Warriors schedule allows, he will be in the stands to watch Butler play in the G League. The Santa Cruz team plays their home opener Friday night and has home games all throughout December, when Butler might be getting close to ready to play. "It may not be for long, but I'm going to play in Santa Cruz," Butler said. "I'm playing in a f-king game." More Warriors - Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already sounding like a media star

nigeria.title: Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo
nigeria.description: Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward. Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer. Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence. “Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters. “The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.” Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number. Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September. Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals. “Nobody can forget Cris’s 23 years in the national team and everything he did,” Jesus told reporters. “I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football.” Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4. nigeria.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. nigeria.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
nigeria.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel. His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez. nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday Tinubu stressed that the Bakassi port would complement, rather than compete with, Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade. “Lagos is not our enemy. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. nigeria.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. nigeria.title: England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run
nigeria.description: Thomas Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarter-final in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added. “I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.” England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley in September, but it might have been a different story had Harry Kane scored a penalty to put Tuchel’s team 3-1 up. “It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.” England players have previously faced racist abuse in Spain, with Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips targeted during a friendly in Madrid in 2004. Spain, meanwhile, must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for supporters singing a discriminatory chant about Muslims during a fixture against Egypt in March. “We will never accept racism,” said Tuchel. “We will never be racist towards anyone.” He added: “I expect, of course, full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. Home mining is not a profit play Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. business.title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday , as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year. Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. The release, like all of the company’s monthly updates, is unaudited and preliminary. Retail pulls back as bitcoin slides The slump in Robinhood’s crypto numbers lines up with a broader retreat by retail traders. Bitcoin ended September near $83,500 and has slid since, falling below $70,000 early Friday for the first time since August as a hot inflation report raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Institutional demand has cooled alongside it. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.description: Everton In Brighton Race For 6ft 5in Defender: Can He Fix Moyes’ Back Line? Everton and Brighton are competing to sign Union Saint-Gilloise centre-back Massiré Sylla, according to Sport Witness , which cites Africa Foot. Both Premier League clubs have already made enquiries for the 21-year-old Senegalese, who also attracted earlier interest from AC Milan and recently signed a new contract at Union running until 2031. Sylla joined from Norwegian side Lyn in January and has since become a regular starter in Belgium. He has played 1,626 minutes across 18 appearances this season, and his market value has jumped to €5m, a little over £4m. At 6ft 5in and right-footed, Sylla wins headers, times his jumps well and threatens at set pieces. He steps out aggressively to win duels, reads danger well enough to intercept, and organises the players around him, with a passing range that includes long diagonals and the occasional line-breaking ball. The weaknesses are just as clear. His tackling can be mistimed, which lets quicker forwards slip past when he commits. He looks loose when a high ball arrives under pressure, and can lose his balance after contact. The Premier League will punish those habits far more often than Belgium does. That profile suits Everton ‘s situation. David Moyes has built a sixth-placed start of 16 points from 10 games on a defence that kept five clean sheets in its first seven league matches, yet James Tarkowski turns 34 next week, Michael Keane is 33, and Jarrad Branthwaite’s hamstring problems keep disrupting his availability. Both clubs are also chasing Atlético Mineiro’s Vitão, an 18-year-old Brazilian centre-back who stands 6ft 4in and won the 2025 CONMEBOL Under-17 Championship. He has only recently broken into Atlético’s senior side. Should Everton make Sylla their priority centre-back target? DUESSELDORF, GERMANY – OCTOBER 22: Massire Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between R. Union Saint-Gilloise and Hapoel Beer-Sheva FC at Merkur Spiel-Arena on October 22, 2026 in Duesseldorf, Germany. (Photo by Pau Barrena/Getty Images) Yes, and they should sign him as a first-team player, not a project. Tarkowski and Keane have both extended their contracts, but neither is getting quicker, and Branthwaite’s record makes him impossible to rely on. Sylla offers Moyes height at set pieces and a front-foot defender. His rash tackling would need coaching out of him, because Premier League wingers exploit a defender who lunges. Vitão is the less sensible chase. An 18-year-old with so little senior experience cannot cover for injuries this season, and Everton shouldn’t tie up a squad place on a player who needs two years. sports.description: Tijjani Reijnders scored three times in the first half as the Dutch thumped Greece (Koen van Weel) Tijjani Reijnders scored a first-half hat-trick as the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 on Friday to move closer to securing a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Crysencio Summerville capitalised on a defensive lapse to give the Dutch an early lead in Amsterdam, before former Manchester City midfielder Reijnders doubled the advantage. Reijnders struck again from close range before completing his hat-trick in the 33rd minute when he squeezed home at the far post. Jurrien Timber turned in a Donyell Malen cross before half-time to make it 5-0, and the Arsenal defender added his second goal of the night on the hour mark. Greece had entered the match unbeaten in Group A2, having taken four points against Germany, and had held a two-goal lead against the Netherlands in October before Reijnders salvaged a 2-2 draw. Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side lead the way with 11 points, three clear of both Greece and Germany, going into the final round of group matches. sports.title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler is sending himself down to the G League for a game
sports.description: Jimmy Butler III of the Golden State Warriors practices during half time of the Warriors game against the Memphis Grizzlies at Chase Center on Oct. 23, 2026, in San Francisco. (Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler says his first game back from his torn ACL will be in the G League. Butler tore his ACL on Jan. 19 and faced a year-long recovery process, but has been ramping up his activity in recent weeks. In an interview with the Athletic's Nick Friedell , Butler said he is planning on playing in a game with the Santa Cruz Warriors, Golden State's affiliate in the NBA minor league, as part of his rehabilitation process. "Well, y'all gonna get your opportunity come Santa Cruz," Butler told the Athletic. "Because I'm definitely coming down there to play. So good luck to everybody. Y'all ain't gonna get too many minutes out of me, but I'm definitely going down there. I want to hoop." Butler even acknowledged that there would be some who may not like the idea. Butler's agent Bernard Lee took to social media to voice his displeasure at Friedell for reporting the story. "Nick…you had to give this table legs huh?" Lee wrote on X . "I'm going to hit you with one of them when I see you." Within the organization, the main person who would be against the idea is Mike Dunleavy, the Warriors general manager and Butler's former teammate with the Bulls. When Friedell asked Butler if he had cleared the plan with Dunleavy, Friedell wrote Butler's smile only got bigger before responding. "I don't got to clear s-t with nobody," Butler said. "I'm going. Me and Mike will fistfight. He's gonna be like, ‘Jimmy, no.' I'm gonna be like, ‘Mike, yes. I'm going to G League, baby!' Y'all know where to find me. Santa Cruz, baby." One person who is clearly in favor of it, though, is Steve Kerr. In an interview with the Athletic in Houston on Wednesday, Kerr celebrated Butler's plans. "I think it makes such perfect sense," Kerr said. "But most guys in the league in Jimmy's position are, like, too vain to do it - and Jimmy's the opposite. I think he would love giving the fans down there a great surprise. That's amazing. I love that." Kerr related the move to how MLB players do rehab assignments in that sport's minor leagues. But while that is quite common in baseball, there has rarely been an NBA player who has done so. Warriors stars Steph Curry and Klay Thompson have both joined the "Sea Dubs" for practices during their recovery processes, but a star of Butler's stature has never played in a G League game. Kerr said if the Warriors schedule allows, he will be in the stands to watch Butler play in the G League. The Santa Cruz team plays their home opener Friday night and has home games all throughout December, when Butler might be getting close to ready to play. "It may not be for long, but I'm going to play in Santa Cruz," Butler said. "I'm playing in a f-king game." More Warriors - Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already sounding like a media star

technology.description: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer. Will DePue, who left the AI giant earlier this year to launch Unemployment Labs, an AI research consultancy, published forensic evidence showing that "DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models." "This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post . "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model." It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea . And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act. On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. technology.description: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). technology.title: Mozilla leaves Solo website owners to go it alone as hosting shuts down
technology.description: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating services – in case all this feels like a bit too much. We suspect that for the sort of technophobes that this was aimed at, it very probably will. Mozilla told The Register : "Experimentation is an important part of Mozilla's mission to make the internet better and give people more choice and control online. Sometimes, that means making the decision to bring a product to an end. Solo will officially shut down on November 30, 2026. We initially notified customers on October 1, providing a 60-day transition period, and have been offering support to help them download their website data and migrate their domains purchased via Solo Domains to another hosting provider." It seems that some 54,000 users were not enough to keep it going, and we can see that this would cost money to keep running. An HTML export is a start, though the FAQ doesn't explain how much work it will take to get a complete, functioning site running elsewhere. Buried in the dark recesses of the web is this vulture's own nearly 30-year-old homepage, created using a mixture of Claris Home Page (which was excellent) and Microsoft FrontPage (ever so slightly less so). We saw what a mess machine-generated web content was back then, and thanks to LLMs, we suspect it is almost infinitely worse now. Mozilla might have made a few bucks by finding a commercial partner to take on its users, and perhaps through them offer a paid site-and-domain transfer service. As we noted last year, it seems not to have negotiated anything with KaiOSTech, which maintains and sells what used to be the formerly FOSS FirefoxOS for use on low-end smartphones.

technology.description: Two email addresses used to send bomb threats that disrupted thousands of Italian schools this week were found exposed in infostealer logs for over a year, experts say. Researchers at Hudson Rock looked into the two university email addresses used to send the bomb threats. One, from Egypt’s Kafrelsheikh University, was scooped up by Vidar – a cybercrime tool that steals saved account credentials and passwords from an infected computer and leaks them to attackers – as far back as October 2021. The other, from Taiwan's Dayeh University, was found among the 284 million addresses included in the massive AlienTXTBASE infostealer dump , dated February 2025. The experts said that the two addresses in infostealer logs do not strictly mean that those behind the bomb threats gained access to the accounts using the previous infostealer compromise. However, it suggests that there was ample time for the universities and Microsoft, which both universities used for authentication, to take action against the accounts that they should have been aware were appearing in infostealer logs. Modern threat intelligence has made infostealer logs highly visible. "Both findings place credential exposure well before the disruption, creating a substantial window in which exposed access could have been investigated and secured," Hudson Rock said . The researchers said that they would need access to details such as the email headers, and data from email providers, including sign-in events and audit records, that could show them more about who sent the email and from what session. Understanding whether the sender authenticated into the account could rule out spoofing, but would not in itself provide proof that the sender used a corresponding password taken from an infostealer log, Hudson Rock noted. There are many ways to get around password-based authentication . The researchers said that in any case where a credential is detected among infostealer logs, the organizations responsible for those accounts must contain them, revoke their access, rotate secrets, and go looking for suspicious activity. "The disruption illustrates why credential exposure deserves attention beyond fraud and data theft," the researchers said. "An account associated with an ordinary university user can become a means of reaching schools, frightening families, and consuming emergency resources."
